vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: adopt-a-caracal
Version: 1.0.0

The skill bundle describes a virtual pet game ('Adopt a Caracal') hosted at animalhouse.ai. The instructions in SKILL.md guide the AI agent to interact with a standard REST API for registration, adoption, and pet care using curl commands. There is no evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or harmful prompt injection; the agent is simply instructed to manage its own game token and perform game-related actions.

llm.summary: The skill is an instruction-only virtual-pet client that only documents how to call animalhouse.ai HTTP APIs and does not request unrelated credentials, installs, or system access.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (virtual Caracal pet) align with the runtime instructions: all examples are curl calls to https://animalhouse.ai describing register/adopt/status/care endpoints. There are no unrelated requirements (no cloud creds, no special binaries).
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md directs the agent to make HTTP requests to the service and to store an auth token returned by that service. It does not instruct reading local files, other env vars, system paths, or sending data to unexpected endpoints. Minor note: it tells users to "store it securely" but does not give guidance on secure storage.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files — instruction-only skill. Nothing is downloaded or written to disk by the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars, credentials, or config paths. The only credential conceptually involved is the service token produced by animalhouse.ai and used in Authorization headers; that is proportional to the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and user-invocable:true. The skill does not request to persist or modify other skills or system-wide settings. Autonomous invocation is allowed by platform default but does not combine here with other red flags.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is coherent with its stated purpose, but consider these practical precautions before using it: verify that https://animalhouse.ai is the real service you expect; understand the returned "your_token" may be long-lived and treat it like a password (store it in a secure secret store, rotate it if possible, and avoid pasting it in public logs); be aware that using the skill causes outbound network calls — anything you include in actions or notes may be transmitted to that service; if you plan to let an autonomous agent use this skill, consider creating a limited/sandbox account on the service rather than your primary account.
